settings.title: Settings
settings.checksHint: Commands the crew runs after every build. They run in the task's worktree with CI=1.
settings.claudeSetupInstall: Install Claude Code in a terminal:
settings.claudeSetupLogin: Run it once and log in when it asks (or type /login):
settings.claudeSetupAccount: Use your Claude subscription (Pro or Max) or an API key from the Claude Console.
settings.claudeSetupRestart: Quit Claude Code and restart Forgeboard. This should then say "available".
settings.claudeSetupNote: Forgeboard uses the Claude Code installed on your machine and never sees your password or key. Without it, use the "Mock (no AI)" crew to try things out.
settings.codexSetupInstall: Install the Codex CLI in a terminal:
settings.codexSetupAccount: Use your ChatGPT account, or an OpenAI API key with codex login --with-api-key.
settings.codexSetupRestart: Restart Forgeboard and pick Codex for an agent in Crew.
settings.codexSetupNote: Forgeboard uses the Codex installed on your machine and never sees your password or key. Codex runs in its own sandbox: Hawk only reads, and Forge only writes inside the task's folder.

runs.empty: No runs in this repository yet.

flows.title: Flows
flows.body: A flow is the list of steps a task goes through before it gets to you: agents that build, checks, agents that review and send work back, and pauses for you.
flows.defaultIn: {count, plural, one {default in # workspace} other {default in # workspaces}}
flows.builtInDescription: Forge builds, the checks run, Hawk reviews and sends it back until it’s right.
flows.name: Name
flows.noSteps: Add a step to see the flow.
flows.checksHint: the repository’s tests, lint and types
flows.askNote: What to check at this pause
flows.askPlaceholder: e.g. Check the copy before the docs are written
flows.endsWithYou: Every flow ends with you: review the change and merge, send it back or discard.
flows.crewNote: Uses the default crew. A workspace with its own crew uses its copy of each agent; agents it doesn’t have come from the default crew.

problem.name: Give the flow a name.
problem.tooMany: A flow can have at most {max} steps.
problem.firstNotBuilder: The first step must be an agent that builds.
problem.unknownAgent: Step {position} uses {name}, who isn’t in the default crew.
problem.sendBackNotBuilder: Step {position} must send work back to a builder before it.
problem.builderSendBack: Step {position} builds, so it can’t send work back.
problem.rounds: Step {position}: rounds must be between 1 and {max}.
problem.leadAlone: A Lead step must be the only step: the Lead plans the rest.
problem.leadRole: Step {position} needs an agent that leads.

flows.leadHint: reads each task and picks who works on it
flows.leadDescription: The Lead reads each task and picks who builds, who reviews and whether the checks run. You approve the plan, or it runs in “Decide and tell me”.

ws.colorHint: The color shows the workspace. Pick one in the sidebar to see only it.
ws.noWorkspacesBody: A workspace groups the repositories of one project, with its own crew and house rules. Your branches stay untouched until you merge.
ws.emptyRepos: This workspace has no repositories yet.

newWs.title: Create workspace
newWs.name: Name
newWs.reposHint: You can add repositories later too.
newWs.crewDefaultHint: Forge and Hawk as they are today. You can customize them later.
newWs.crewCopyHint: Reuse a crew you've already tuned.
newWs.rulesHint: General house rules always apply in every workspace.
newWs.crewTeamHint: One of your teams, or a ready-made one.

wsSettings.title: Configure workspace
wsSettings.repoHint: A repository belongs to one workspace. Moving it keeps its history.
wsSettings.removeRepoConfirm: Remove {repo} from Forgeboard? Its tasks are removed; the folder isn't touched.
wsSettings.crewDefaultHint: Changes to the default crew apply here too.
wsSettings.crewCustomHint: Tune each agent just for this workspace.
wsSettings.rulesHint: Workspace rules apply to all its repositories. Repository rules apply only there.
wsSettings.deleteConfirm: Delete "{name}"? Its tasks and rules are removed; your repositories on disk aren't touched.
wsSettings.dangerHint: Archiving hides the workspace and keeps its history. Deleting removes its tasks and rules; your repositories aren't touched.
wsSettings.cmdStandardHint: Edits files and runs npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, npx and node to install and test. In practice this can run any code on your machine: use it on repositories you trust.
wsSettings.cmdRestrictedHint: Only edits files and uses git and ls to read. No commands: Forgeboard runs the checks afterwards and sends back any failures.
wsSettings.safetyNote: Agents that review never change files or run commands, in either mode. With Codex, its sandbox also keeps agents that build from writing outside the task's folder; in Restricted they have no network (commands still run, isolated).
wsSettings.askHint: Applies to every task in this workspace.
wsSettings.askAskHint: Stops and waits for your answer. Good when a wrong guess is costly, like data or public API changes.
wsSettings.askDecideHint: Goes with its best guess and lists what it decided. Correct it in the conversation or at review. Only stops when a wrong guess would be destructive.
wsSettings.planFirst: {name} shows a plan before big tasks
wsSettings.planFirstHint: When a task touches several files or layers, the steps show up for you to adjust before it starts.
wsSettings.interruptHint: Your message arrives right away: the agent stops its step and resumes with it. Off, it waits for the next pause. You can switch it on each message.
wsSettings.notify: Notify me in the browser when I'm needed
wsSettings.notifyHint: A system notification when an agent asks something or finishes review, if Forgeboard isn't on screen. For this browser.
wsSettings.flowHint: New tasks in this workspace run this flow, unless you pick another in the task bar.
wsSettings.crewTeamHint: Agents, Lead and default flow come from that team.
wsSettings.crewTeamNone: No teams yet: create one in Teams.
